unclaimed_findings: U1. `--observe` is the property the class survives in most visibly. Executed against the repository's own `.github/workflows/verify.yml`: writing the flag into the candidate step's `name:` and leaving `run: python scripts/verify.py` bare passes all 37 cases, and `yaml.safe_load` confirms the runner would execute a bare verifier. For that spelling `if-no-files-found: error` still fails the upload at runtime, loudly. The aggravated form does not: `run: |` with `echo "[]" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/candidate-observations.json"` on one line and `echo skipping --observe "$RUNNER_TEMP/candidate-observations.json"` on the next, then a bare verifier, passes all 37 cases AND satisfies the runtime check, because the named file exists and holds `[]`. That is a green CI run whose retained artifact is a fabrication and whose verifier never wrote a record. Reading `--observe` out of `keys_of(step).get('run', '')`, plus the existing folded/literal block handling, is what would put it on the footing the other properties already have.

U2. `continue-on-error` is read by regex where `keys_of` was already available and already correct. `- continue-on-error: true` as the keeper's first key passes all 37 cases on the real verify.yml; `keys_of(keeper)` returns it, `continues_on_error` never asks. And `before_steps(block)` stops at `steps:`, so a job-level `continue-on-error: true` written after the steps list passes whenever the keeper is not the last step - also executed on the real verify.yml, also 37 OK, also confirmed by `yaml.safe_load`. Each of these removes the entirety of the runtime enforcement, which is the thing the module's own comment says the key neuters. Neither was reported by any of the four prior witnesses; both are new at this reading.

U3. The head commit's own summary overstates in the same two places. 'Requested outcome: no property of a step is read anywhere but at its own key' is not what the code does. 'Remaining substring reads, all deliberate and all failing closed: `<<` marks a heredoc, and the verifier's own name is matched lexically' enumerates two and misses two, and the two it misses are the two that fail open. The prior commit's title, 'read the flag off the command', names a repair the code did not make: `decomment` strips comments, and the flag is still searched over the step's whole text. This is recorded because the claim is the artifact here as much as the code is.

U4. `decomment` tracks quotes; a YAML plain scalar does not. For `- run: python scripts/verify.py ' # --observe "$RUNNER_TEMP/obs.json"`, `yaml.safe_load` resolves the run value to `python scripts/verify.py '` - a bare verifier - while `decomment` sees an unclosed quote, keeps the rest of the line, and finds the flag. Same with a double quote. The divergence fails open only into U1, because keeping more text can only ADD mentions and `<<` markers, which over-refuse. It is a distinct reader defect from U1 and is undeclared.

U5. `under_temp` accepts `path: $RUNNER_TEMP/obs.json` as naming the same file as `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/obs.json`. GitHub Actions does not expand shell variables in a `with:` input, so only the second names the file. The guard accepts a keeper that cannot find its file; `if-no-files-found: error` catches it at runtime, noisily. Minor, fails open in the guard and closed at runtime, and undeclared.
U6. `graded` in `unretained` is assigned, incremented, and never read. Dead local in a graded production module; lint does not reach it.

U7. `scripts/tests/test_repository_ci_workflows.py` is now 417 lines. `is_production` is False for it because of the `/tests/` segment, so the ceiling still does not see it.
